title: Lift a specified finite-set fibre equivalence to finite left modules.
statement:
/-- Lift a specified finite-set fibre equivalence to finite left modules.
Source: Stacks Project, Tag 0DV5 (3), proof; the proof of
`cor-galois-lisse-representations`, step 1.

Exact Lean statement:
theorem galois_lisse_finite_module_lift
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y) (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [∀ P, MulAction G ((FiniteEtale.fiber y).obj P)] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
    (Φ : Y.FiniteEtale ≌ Y.FLC) (E : Y.FLC ≌ ContAction FintypeCat.{u} G)
    (γ : G ≃ₜ* Aut (ObjectProperty.ι (IsLisseEtaleSheafOfSets (T := Y)) ⋙
      (pointSmallEtale y).sheafFiber (A := Type (u + 1))))
    (η : Φ.functor ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙
      (pointSmallEtale y).sheafFiber (A := Type (u + 1)) ≅
      FiniteEtale.fiber y ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget FintypeCat.{u} ⋙
        uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u})
    (τ : E.functor ⋙ forget₂ (ContAction FintypeCat.{u} G) FintypeCat.{u} ⋙
      CategoryTheory.forget FintypeCat.{u} ⋙ uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u} ≅
      ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙ (pointSmallEtale y).sheafFiber (A := Type (u + 1)))
    (hτ : ∀ (F : Y.FLC) (g : G) (z : ULift.{u + 1} (E.functor.obj F).obj.V),
      τ.hom.app F ⟨((E.functor.obj F).obj.ρ g).hom z.down⟩ =
        (γ g).hom.app F (τ.hom.app F z)) :
    ∃ (e : ∀ (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [Ring Λ] [Finite Λ],
        LisseModuleSheafCategory Y Λ ≌ galoisFiniteRepresentations Λ G)
      (τM : ∀ (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [Ring Λ] [Finite Λ],
        (e Λ).functor ⋙ ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙
          forget₂ (Rep.{u + 1} Λ G) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) ≅
        ObjectProperty.ι _ ⋙ (pointSmallEtale y).sheafFiber (A := ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)),
      galoisFiniteEvaluationAction y G ⟨γ, Φ, η, e, τM⟩

proof.text:
*(1): the equivalence.* Write $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ for the finite locally constant sheaves of sets on $Y_{\Et}$ and $\pi_1\text{-}\mathbf{Set}$ for finite sets with a continuous $\pi_1$-action. By [thm-galois-lc-etale] (finite locally constant sheaves are the sheaves represented by finite etale $Y$-schemes, compatibly with the fibre functors) and [thm-galois-fundamental] ($Y$ connected), the fibre functor $F_{\bar y}:\mathcal A\mapsto\mathcal A_{\bar y}$, with $\pi_1=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y})$ acting by evaluation [def-galois-fibre-functor], is an equivalence $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)\to\pi_1\text{-}\mathbf{Set}$ compatible with finite limits, in particular with finite products and the final object. By [lem-pod-lisse-module-sheaves-as-module-objects], a locally constant sheaf of finite left $\Lambda$-modules is the same as a $\Lambda$-module object of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ (its underlying sheaf of sets with the maps $+$, $0$, $-$, $\lambda\cdot$), and $\Lambda$-linear maps are the maps of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ commuting with these. By [lem-pod-equivalence-induces-module-objects] (1), $F_{\bar y}$ induces an equivalence of $\Lambda$-module objects, and by (2) of that lemma the $\Lambda$-module objects of $\pi_1\text{-}\mathbf{Set}$ are the finite left $\Lambda$-modules with a continuous $\Lambda$-linear $\pi_1$-action. The composite sends $\mathcal F$ to the finite set $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ with the operations $(+)_{\bar y},(\lambda\cdot)_{\bar y}$, which are the module operations of the stalk of $\mathcal F$ as a sheaf of modules (the stalk is a filtered colimit of sections and filtered colimits of sets commute with finite products), with $\sigma$ acting as in the statement. This is the asserted equivalence; it is additive, because the addition on $\operatorname{Hom}$ is computed by $+$ on both sides. Formalization subproblem: identify lisse module sheaves with module objects using
`lisseToModuleObject_isIso_of_categories`. Rewrite the diagram axioms of
`ModuleObjectStruct` as the generalized-element axioms of `InternalModule` and
lift the set equivalence with `equivalence_induces_internalModules`.
Use `internalModules_finiteContAction` to obtain continuous finite modules,
flatten the two full subcategories, and lift the finite carrier to universe u+1.
The fibre comparison is linear because the transported addition and scalar maps
are their maps on stalks. The set and module stalks agree by the filtered-colimit
forgetful comparison, whose germ formula gives the stated kappa. Naturality of
the specified set comparison gives the evaluation-action formula.

mathlib_searches.query: An equivalence between finite locally constant module sheaves and finite continuous representations, compatible with stalks and tensor products
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits, primarily Mathlib.Condensed.Discrete.Module; no scheme-etale or adic correspondence. Earlier fundamental-group query found the abstract functorToContAction equivalence only.

mathlib_searches.query: Integral adic sheaves and continuous finite dimensional p-adic representations, tensor products and scalar extension
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits on AdicCompletion, including ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian, but no sheaf-representation equivalence or monoidal comparison.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Useful finite-module infrastructure already covered by the declared adic-limit dependency; no exact match.

mathlib_searches.results: LocalSystems proves the finite commutative-ring equivalence; it does not cover all noncommutative finite rings nor the adic clauses. EquivalenceInternalModule proves transport of internal modules, and its finite-action identification is stated. No adic-category equivalence was found.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Reuse the declared modules for the parts they cover; the missing comparison/glue is stated here.
